input.question: What's the maximum height a fly or a mosquito can reach?
input.ground_truth: [National Geographic Article about bumble bees](_URL_0_) I mention bumble bees because they were studied a lot by scientists. Some people thought bumble bees shouldn't be able to fly because they are too heavy, so they ran a lot of tests on them! Helicopters have an upper limit of height in which they can safely fly because as you go higher, the atmosphere thins. Less air, means less lift. The same goes for insects! To answer your question directly, there is no absolute value at which insects can reach, but bumble bees can fly higher than Mt Everest. Flies, and other fast flying swift insects could reach those heights as well, but they have no need to. They have extra power, so they can carry pollen, nectar, eggs, fly quickly and efficiently at low altitudes.

If you imagine the sky as a big stack of books, a fly or mosquito can only fly as high as maybe the top one or two books. That’s not very high! Usually, they fly close to the ground, like around your head or on your food.

So, the highest a fly or mosquito can go is maybe as tall as a person or a little tree, but not as high as a tall building or a mountain. They like to stay close to the ground where they can find food and places to rest.
